data.title: Seera Holding Group (TADAWUL:1810) Just Released Its Third-Quarter Earnings: Here's What Analysts Think
data.description:
Last week saw the newest third-quarter earnings release from Seera Holding Group (TADAWUL:1810), an important milestone in the company's journey to build a stronger business. Results look mixed - while revenue fell marginally short of analyst estimates at ر.س1.1b, statutory earnings were in line with expectations, at ر.س0.17 per share. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. We thought readers would find it interesting to see the analysts latest (statutory) post-earnings forecasts for next year.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Taking into account the latest results, the consensus forecast from Seera Holding Group's four analysts is for revenues of ر.س4.99b in 2027. This reflects a solid 12% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to leap 76% to ر.س0.69. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of ر.س5.02b and earnings per share (EPS) of ر.س0.79 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become more bearish following the latest results. While there were no changes to revenue forecasts, there was a real cut to EPS estimates.

View our latest analysis for Seera Holding Group

It might be a surprise to learn that the consensus price target was broadly unchanged at ر.س23.40, with the analysts clearly implying that the forecast decline in earnings is not expected to have much of an impact on valuation. It could also be instructive to look at the range of analyst estimates, to evaluate how different the outlier opinions are from the mean. Currently, the most bullish analyst values Seera Holding Group at ر.س27.30 per share, while the most bearish prices it at ر.س20.00. As you can see, analysts are not all in agreement on the stock's future, but the range of estimates is still reasonably narrow, which could suggest that the outcome is not totally unpredictable.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. It's pretty clear that there is an expectation that Seera Holding Group's revenue growth will slow down substantially, with revenues to the end of 2027 expected to display 9.1% growth on an annualised basis. This is compared to a historical growth rate of 24% over the past five years. Juxtapose this against the other companies in the industry with analyst coverage, which are forecast to grow their revenues (in aggregate) 7.2% per year. So it's pretty clear that, while Seera Holding Group's revenue growth is expected to slow, it's still expected to grow faster than the industry itself.

The Bottom Line

The most important thing to take away is that the analysts downgraded their earnings per share estimates, showing that there has been a clear decline in sentiment following these results. Happily, there were no major changes to revenue forecasts, with the business still expected to grow faster than the wider industry. The consensus price target held steady at ر.س23.40, with the latest estimates not enough to have an impact on their price targets.

data.title: Dar AlBalad for Business Solutions' (TADAWUL:7205) Weak Earnings May Only Reveal A Part Of The Whole Picture
data.description:

Zooming In On Dar AlBalad for Business Solutions' Earnings

Many investors haven't heard of the accrual ratio from cashflow, but it is actually a useful measure of how well a company's profit is backed up by free cash flow (FCF) during a given period. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, Dar AlBalad for Business Solutions had an accrual ratio of 0.29. We can therefore deduce that its free cash flow fell well short of covering its statutory profit, suggesting we might want to think twice before putting a lot of weight on the latter. Indeed, in the last twelve months it reported free cash flow of ر.س3.8m, which is significantly less than its profit of ر.س48.1m. We note, however, that Dar AlBalad for Business Solutions grew its free cash flow over the last year.

data.title: MOBI Industry Co. (TADAWUL:9517) Is About To Go Ex-Dividend, And It Pays A 3.6% Yield
data.description:
MOBI Industry Co. (TADAWUL:9517) stock is about to trade ex-dividend in 3 days. The ex-dividend date generally occurs two days before the record date, which is the day on which shareholders need to be on the company's books in order to receive a dividend. The ex-dividend date is of consequence because whenever a stock is bought or sold, the trade can take two business days or more to settle. Meaning, you will need to purchase MOBI Industry's shares before the 23rd of November to receive the dividend, which will be paid on the 6th of December.

The company's next dividend payment will be ر.س0.15 per share. Last year, in total, the company distributed ر.س0.60 to shareholders. Last year's total dividend payments show that MOBI Industry has a trailing yield of 3.6% on the current share price of ر.س16.75. If you buy this business for its dividend, you should have an idea of whether MOBI Industry's dividend is reliable and sustainable. So we need to investigate whether MOBI Industry can afford its dividend, and if the dividend could grow.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Dividends are usually paid out of company profits, so if a company pays out more than it earned then its dividend is usually at greater risk of being cut. That's why it's good to see MOBI Industry paying out a modest 39% of its earnings. A useful secondary check can be to evaluate whether MOBI Industry generated enough free cash flow to afford its dividend. MOBI Industry paid out more free cash flow than it generated - 183%, to be precise - last year, which we think is concerningly high. It's hard to consistently pay out more cash than you generate without either borrowing or using company cash, so we'd wonder how the company justifies this payout level.

While MOBI Industry's dividends were covered by the company's reported profits, cash is somewhat more important, so it's not great to see that the company didn't generate enough cash to pay its dividend. Were this to happen repeatedly, this would be a risk to MOBI Industry's ability to maintain its dividend.

View our latest analysis for MOBI Industry

Click here to see how much of its profit MOBI Industry paid out over the last 12 months.

Have Earnings And Dividends Been Growing?

Companies with consistently growing earnings per share generally make the best dividend stocks, as they usually find it easier to grow dividends per share. Investors love dividends, so if earnings fall and the dividend is reduced, expect a stock to be sold off heavily at the same time. For this reason, we're glad to see MOBI Industry's earnings per share have risen 17% per annum over the last five years. Earnings have been growing at a decent rate, but we're concerned dividend payments consumed most of the company's cash flow over the past year.

The main way most investors will assess a company's dividend prospects is by checking the historical rate of dividend growth. MOBI Industry has delivered an average of 25% per year annual increase in its dividend, based on the past five years of dividend payments. It's exciting to see that both earnings and dividends per share have grown rapidly over the past few years.

Final Takeaway

From a dividend perspective, should investors buy or avoid MOBI Industry? We're glad to see the company has been improving its earnings per share while also paying out a low percentage of income. However, it's not great to see it paying out what we see as an uncomfortably high percentage of its cash flow. In summary, it's hard to get excited about MOBI Industry from a dividend perspective.

So while MOBI Industry looks good from a dividend perspective, it's always worthwhile being up to date with the risks involved in this stock. For instance, we've identified 3 warning signs for MOBI Industry (1 doesn't sit too well with us) you should be aware of.

With fresh information on performance fee revenue now in the market, the question is how much of the recent share price slide is tied to shifts in the underlying profit story versus changing sentiment.

Is Regal Partners Still Cheap on Earnings?

P/E fits Regal Partners because earnings are the key swing factor for an asset manager that relies on both base fees and performance fees. On this measure, Regal Partners trades on a P/E of about 3.7x, which is far below the broader Capital Markets industry average of roughly 19.1x and also well under the peer group at about 36.2x. That is a steep markdown in how the market is pricing each dollar of current earnings compared with other listed investment firms.

The Fair Ratio model, which adjusts the target multiple for Regal Partners' forecast return on equity, balance sheet and risk profile, points to a higher P/E than where the shares trade today. On this framework, the current 3.7x screens as undervalued. Because management has already recognised A$122.7m of crystallised performance fees in 2026 and flagged limited additional fees for the second half, the low multiple suggests investors are heavily discounting the durability of that earnings line. data.title: Aircraft Deal Might Change The Case For Investing In GE Stock
data.description:
• General Electric, through GE Aerospace, recently participated in a US$12b aircraft deal with Philippine Airlines alongside Boeing, supplying engines and long-term services for the carrier’s future fleet.
  • The agreement underscores the scale of GE Aerospace’s installed base and service pipeline, reinforcing how large multiyear engine contracts can shape workload, capital needs, and long-term aftermarket revenue visibility.
  • The focus now is on how General Electric's refined aerospace investment narrative incorporates this Philippine Airlines engine deal and what that means for future cash generation and execution risk.
Activate your watchlist with General Electric's latest aerospace moves and compare them with hand-picked peers in the 44 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks.

General Electric Investment Narrative Recap

To own General Electric, you need to be comfortable with a concentrated aviation story built on a large installed base and long service contracts, while accepting exposure to airframe partners and heavy R&D. The near term swing factor remains execution in commercial engines and services, particularly how efficiently GE converts its reported US$52.6b of revenue into cash while managing supply chain constraints.

The biggest current operational risk is still tied to Boeing production issues, as highlighted by Zdend, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, who flags GE’s dependence on new aircraft deliveries for its future installed base. Recent headlines around building demolition and site clean up look immaterial to that cash and delivery equation.

The most relevant recent item for potential catalysts is the Industrial Select Sector SPDR ETF lifting its GE exposure to 6.38% of assets. That change does not alter the underlying business. However, it reinforces how central GE Aerospace has become within the US industrial complex at a time when earnings are forecast to grow 10.21% a year and the P/E of 36.8x reflects a high level of execution success already in the price.

This heightened ETF presence could increase trading attention around key operational milestones, especially any updates on R&D spend for next generation engines that Zdend views as a major future cash demand. It also sharpens the focus on whether management can keep earnings quality high while carrying a significant debt load and funding large development programs without eroding that aerospace centric thesis.

Zdend sets a US$307.00 fair value for General Electric as the result of GE Aerospace’s concentrated aviation focus, its large commercial engine and services backlog, and the long-duration, contract-based cash flows generated by its aftermarket model and perceived pricing power.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One alternate view on General Electric focuses on margin risk. The most bearish analysts were modeling revenue of about US$62.2b and earnings of US$11.1b by 2029, then applying a 34.1x P/E, which is less optimistic than consensus. Those forecasts came before the Philippine Airlines deal, so expectations could still shift.
